newsitem.title: UK: Copper ends LME off highest for over two months.
newsitem.headline: Copper ends LME off highest for over two months.

text.p: Copper prices settled back from the highest levels since September 3 during LME kerb trading on Tuesday, but the market still ended firmer and poised for further gains, traders said.

Business slackened during the kerb, and with some expected profit-taking emerging, prices dipped back under $2,050, a slightly unconstructive close, although the technical trend remains upwards, they said.
The initial factors behind Tuesday's strength was the 4,225-tonne fall in stocks, which although expected, brought inventories to six-year lows of 109,175 tonnes.

But the spreads also tightened, with cash/threes moving above $90 backwardation at one stage, while option-related buying kicked in when $2,045/50 resistance was cleared. The inventory declines continue to puzzle the market, which is unsure whether metal is moving into consumption or being switched to bonded warehouses. However, with LME stocks at such low levels the backwardation is seen remaining firm and reaching $100 soon. It was indicated at $80/90 by the close.
Three months prices closed at $2,045, off the $2,057 peak, but still $33 above Monday's kerb. The next objective is $2,070.

Fundamental stimulus for copper's strength emanated from the lack of Chinese selling, as well as a severe drought in central Chile, which could have an impact on production on Codelco's El Teniente mine and Exxon Mineral's Los Bronces facility.

Aluminium business was less active, with the market a reluctant partner in the copper rally. Prices inched up above $1,460 but failed to locate buy stops nearer $1,470, and subsequently slipped back to end at $1,454.50, up $6.50. Some traders said the increase Final kerb business was at $7,230, up $30 a tonne from Monday.

Lead came back from its peak of $740, to close at $737, up $5, while zinc finished with a $4 gain at $1,064. Both markets traded routinely, but were buttressed to some extent by the strength of copper, traders said.

Tin continued to push higher this afternoon, against a background of a 115-tonne inventory decline, hitting a peak of $6,000 before closing the session at $5,980, up from the previous finish of $5,925.
The alloy market was marked higher with primary, and ended at $1,305/1,308, up from Monday's $1,295 close.
